Subject: Intro + sequencing for private deployment (Equinox)

Samir/Dana —

Thanks again for the productive technical discovery last week. Per our plan to run a short pilot for the edge gateway + private endpoint configuration, I’m looping in Markus (implementation lead) and Laura (Eng Ops) to own sequencing and the network runbook.

Primary goals for the pilot:
- Establish VPC peering between Equinox VPC (eu-west-1) and Redwood private peering mesh
- Provision private endpoints for the inference control plane and metrics streams
- Validate on-prem appliance onboarding (certificate exchange + outbound connectivity rules)

Attachments: equinox-edge-ip-list.csv (IP ranges we asked you to confirm), onprem-hardware-specs.pdf

Next steps: Markus will propose a sequencing checklist and a 2-hour validation call. Could you confirm availability for a window on Friday 12/18 (EU morning)? Also please confirm whether your org requires static source IP ranges for the control plane or if NAT is allowed.

Thanks,
Monica

Subject: Re: Intro + sequencing for private deployment (Equinox)

Samir/Dana — thanks, will hold 09:30–11:30 UTC on 2026-12-18 for a validation call. Draft sequencing below (high level) — please review and flag gaps: 

1) Pre-call (this week)
   - Equinox confirms static egress IPs (or final ranges) and uploads firewall rules
   - Share CSR details if you require a mutual TLS onboarding
   - Redwood provides: control-plane FQNs, TLS fingerprint, and expected ports (443, 5222 for metrics agent)
2) Call: connectivity validation (2 hrs)
   - VPC peering handshake checks (route propagation + security groups)
   - Establish private endpoints and confirm DNS resolution from Equinox VPC
   - On-prem appliance initial bootstrap (cert exchange, heartbeat-to-control-plane)
   - Smoke test: tokenized request to sample model and metrics ingest check
3) Pilot week (staging)
   - Run 2-hour load window during off-peak; monitor latency and KV cache warming
   - Confirm automatic fallback path (hosted variant) in case of failure
4) Cutover window (production move)
   - Scheduled two-week notice + rollback plan

Open items for Equinox:
- Final /24s for firewall (list attached)
- Whether outbound is via NAT gateway (single IP) or via multiple static IPs from appliances
- Contact for your internal PKI team (for signed certs)

I’ll turn this into a short checklist before the call. In the meantime, Laura — can you share the appliance bootstrap guide and the private-endpoint-checklist so Samir’s team can pre-validate?

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Intro + sequencing for private deployment (Equinox)

Hi team — attaching the appliance bootstrap guide and a lightweight checklist for the private endpoints. A few clarifications from our side:

- Appliance egress: outbound connections to Redwood control plane must be allowed on 443 (TLS) and TCP 5222 (metric stream). Keep connections outbound only; no inbound firewall rules are required for the appliance.
- TLS: we support both mutual TLS and server-side TLS. If you want mTLS, please share your CA certchain (PEM) and we will generate a CSR flow.
- DNS: private endpoints use split-horizon DNS. On your VPC side make sure the private hosted zone is configured to forward to Redwood’s resolver.
- Monitoring: we will push a metrics agent that uses an outbound port (5222) and requires an allowlist entry for the control-plane FQNs (provided on the call).

Attachments: onprem-hardware-specs.pdf, private-endpoint-checklist.xlsx

See you on Friday.

Laura Bennett
Staff Engineer, Eng Ops — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Thanks all — summary from today’s session and agreed actions: 

- Equinox will finalize the two TBD /24s by EOD Monday (12/20) and upload to the Drive folder.
- Equinox IT will provide PKI contact and CA chain for mTLS if we choose mutual auth during pilot (tentative: yes).
- Redwood to provide a consolidated runbook with command snippets for route checks, DNS resolution steps, and the certificate exchange flow by 12/17 EOD (Markus owner).
- Pilot load window scheduled for week of 2027-01-04; exact date TBD once firewall ranges are confirmed.

No blockers from our side beyond the IP confirmation and PKI contact. Appreciated the clear sequencing — feel free to add any prescriptive rollback notes to the runbook.

Samir
